Unfortunately, letting the agreement expire is often a significant mistake because it gives an opportunity for your confidential information to be used against your business.
According to Harvard, you could introduce exceptions that would make them expire right when your information is publicly disclosed, for instance, at a public event.
You could also implement this with an “opt-out” option, which, according to the American Bar Association, would only permit the receiving party to opt-out by following a specific process.
According to the team at the Chicago Tribune, you could also have another term, which is similar to “opt-out three-months after consummating the purpose of the agreement.” While both of these have their merits, you could also consider agreeing to automatically renew the agreement.
